medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Tulane University School of Medicine values diversity. Tulane defines diversity broadly to include: persons of color, members of the LGBTQIA community, members of diverse ethnic groups including those typically underrepresented in medicine, members of economically disadvantaged groups, and any others who bring a different perspective to the learning environment. The school of medicine believes in a rich educational experience for all students through the infusion of cultural competency, sensitivity, and attentiveness. Special activities available for, but not limited to, students from groups underrepresented in medicine participate in efforts to advocate for communities within New Orleans through community service, education, and health advocacy projects. This effort will generate conscientious global citizens primed to provide vital medical care to the diverse population in southeastern Louisiana and around the globe, thus advancing health equity.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of absence will generally be granted for one year and may be requested for one additional year.  Requests are to be made directly to the  Associate Dean for Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Outside of the classroom, TUSOM students have an opportunity to become involved in a variety of opportunities and experiences.  From a student’s physical and mental well-being to enhancing their academic experience and their career, TUSOM supports their students throughout their medical education journey. These experiences allow students to continue to follow the passions they had before they started medical school and help develop leadership, embrace inclusion, and assist with the development of the competence needed to provide exceptional clinical care and service to the community. TUSOM has a commitment towards improving the New Orleans community.  As such, community involvement and service is an integral part of student life.  Students volunteer in a variety of clinical settings and work in the community as educators, advocates, and leaders.  For more information regarding student clubs and organizations: https://som-d9work.tulane.edu/form/ask-a-medical-student
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Tulane University School of Medicine is located in downtown New Orleans, a few blocks from the New Orleans Superdome and the French Quarter.
Famed for its history, music and cuisine, New Orleans is one of the world's most extraordinary cities. Star-studded events like Mardi Gras and Jazz Fest draw thousands of visitors to the city each year. Unique neighborhoods reflect the city's French, Spanish and Caribbean roots. World-class museums display renowned artworks and artifacts. Shopping options range from vintage shops and antique stores to high-end boutiques and galleries. Sports fans can find something to cheer for year-round with New Orleans' many professional teams. The educational experience at Tulane University is interwoven with this rich cultural tapestry.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Reasonably priced housing of all kinds is widely available, including the Deming Pavilion student residence, which is adjacent to the Tulane University Hospital and Clinic and across the street from the medical school.
For more information about living in New Orleans: https://medicine.tulane.edu/admissions/living-new-orleans
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Tulane University School of Medicine supports and fosters an inclusive campus community. For more information visit the Office of Multicultural Affairs at: https://medicine.tulane.edu/office-multicultural-affairs or Tulane's Medical Student Pride Alliance at: https://tmedweb.tulane.edu/clubs/mspa/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Tulane University School of Medicine offers its students a variety of wellness programs and support services. These include a counseling center, mental health care platform, the Mayo Well-Being Index, and the "Wave of Support" program.  A combination of Tulane medical students, faculty, and individuals affiliated with the medical community work together with each other to achieve offer wellness and support for TUSOM students. https://medicine.tulane.edu/wellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Tulane University School of Medicine takes on the culture of the community it resides in, New Orleans.  Much like our most hospitable city, our medical school fosters a sense of service to others, inclusion and collaboration.  Students are motivated to pursue their medical interest while continuing to pursue the activities that give them passion and purpose.  From their first day on campus, our medical students are encouraged to enjoy their medical education journey while looking out for one another.  This allows our students to become competent, compassionate, and innovative healthcare leaders.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: While a personal vehicle is not required, Tulane University School of Medicine strongly recommends for their students to have a personal vehicle, especially during the third and fourth years of medical school training.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Tutors are available through the Office of Medical Education.  Office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:30-5 pm.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures combined with Team Based Learning and Case Based Learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are placed in tertiles at the end of their third year for MSPE purposes.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Most lectures are optional as lectures are livestreamed and recorded for later viewing.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Tulane University School of Medicine’s MD curriculum is a comprehensive, four-year program designed to build strong clinical and scientific foundations while preparing students for residency and beyond. The curriculum begins with Phase I, focusing on normal structure and function through systems-based modules that integrate anatomy, physiology, histology, and foundational sciences. In Phase II, students explore disease mechanisms and therapeutic approaches across organ systems, incorporating clinical skills, pathology, pharmacology, and case-based learning. The third year emphasizes hands-on clinical experience through core clerkships in hospital and outpatient settings. In the final year, students refine their clinical skills with advanced electives, acting internships, and required rotations in emergency medicine, radiology, and community health. Tulane also offers combined degree programs such as MD/MPH, MD/MBA, and MD/PhD for students seeking additional training in public health, business, or research.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Although Tulane has a commitment to the community, Tulane does not aim to train one type of physician.  Our philosophy is to train service minded physicians who are prepared to enter the medical work place of the future.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: TUSOM students have plenty of opportunities available for getting involved in research, which include basic/bench research, clinical/translational research, population/public health research, and medical education research. Strong research programs exist in cardiovascular, lung, kidney and stem cell biology.  Medical students can apply for the Michael DeBakey Honors Program to begin research in their first year and continue throughout medical school.  Also, students can apply for the ASPIRE Summer Research Fellowship for research between their first and second year. However, students can get involved with research at any time during their medical education. For more information regarding student research, visit: https://medicine.tulane.edu/research/student-research
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Visit this link for more information regarding the TUSOM curriculum: https://medicine.tulane.edu/undergraduate-medical-education/curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service learning (community service) is required during the first two years.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: TUSOM has affiliation agreements with more than 10 hospitals & clinics in New Orleans and other communities in the state; three of its principal clinical teaching facilities are in close proximity.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Founded nearly 200 years ago by physicians responding to a yellow fever epidemic, Tulane University School of Medicine remains one of the nation’s most recognized centers for medical education. TUSOM is a vibrant center for education, research and public service.  As the second oldest medical school in the South and the 15th oldest medical school in the United States, TUSOM maintains more than 20 community student-led clinics throughout New Orleans, providing quality healthcare to the underserved population. Leading groundbreaking work in infectious diseases, cardiovascular health, cancer, and neuroscience, TUSOM continues to shape the future of medicine both locally and globally. On a daily basis, we strive to meet our mission of "Education, Research and Patient Care: We Heal Communities."
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We improve human health and foster healthy communities through discovery and translation of the best science into clinical practice and education; to deliver the highest quality patient care and prepare the next generation of distinguished clinical and scientific leaders.
medSchoolInformation.videoTitle: Why Tulane University School of Medicine?

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Tulane's requirement for letters of recommendation is as follows: 
1) A committee letter or a letter of recommendation packet from your pre-medical advising committee or 2) A total of three letters of recommendation.  It is best to choose letters from people who know you best and can speak on either your academic ability, your commitment to service, or your passion for medicine.  These letters can be from anyone of your choice, but at least one must come from someone with a science/medical background.   
If you are out of school or your undergraduate degree is not science based, then choose three professionals that know you well.
For a committee letter with three or more signatures, no additional letters are needed. Do not submit more than three letters total, if sending individual letters. We prefer no more than three LORs.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
TUSOM reviews applicants for admissions using a holistic review process.  This review process considers a range of characteristics and experiences that are aligned with TUSOM’s mission and values.  
Academic achievements are important; however, we feel that academic metrics such as test scores and grades do not entirely give an accurate description of a candidate’s character, personal journey, resilience, nor their alignment with our mission and values.  Someone’s personal attributes, self-reflection, and their path to medicine show qualities that academic metrics may not.  
In our holistic admissions process, an individual’s academic metrics are considered in the context of the applicant and in a larger framework of their lived experiences.  
•    Commitment to service- In this commitment, what did you learn about the community you served?  What did you learn about yourself?
•    Passion for medicine- On your journey toward medicine, what opportunities did you pursue?  How did these experiences shape your view of medicine?  Once again, what did you learn about yourself?
•    Maturity- How have your past experiences taught you about resiliency and adaptability?  How has adversity shaped you into the person you are today and want to be in the future?
•    Leadership- What lessons have you learned by being a leader?  What traits have you learned from being a follower of a good leader?
•    How does your values or your “mission in medicine” align with TUSOM’s mission and values?
Academic Metrics
As mentioned, TUSOM practices a holistic admission review process.  We do not have any minimum GPA requirements or MCAT thresholds to receive a TUSOM secondary application or to receive an interview invitation.  With that being said, we do review applicant’s academic history to ensure they can complete our medical curriculum without any delays.  
Applicants with MCAT scores and undergraduate GPA withing the following ranges are encouraged to apply to our program:
•    An MCAT Total of 497-500 (40th-50th percentile) and an undergraduate GPA of 3.80 or higher
•    An MCAT total of 500-504 (50th-62nd percentile) and an undergraduate GPA of 3.60 or higher
•    An MCAT total of 505 (65th percentile) and above with an undergraduate GPA of 3.30 or higher
Only an applicant's total cumulative undergraduate GPA as calculated by AMCAS will be considered with their application. Post-Baccalaureate GPA is factored into the undergraduate GPA.  An applicant’s graduate GPA will be considered and can help in the academic review process.
All applicants are required to take the MCAT within three (3) years of the year of the application cycle or four (4) years of their matriculation to medical school.
Beginning April 30, accepted applicants have the option to “Commit to Enroll” at TUSOM. When an applicant selects “Commit to Enroll” to TUSOM, they should notify all other institutions where they hold an acceptance or position on the waitlist that they wish to withdraw their acceptance or position on the waitlist from that school. TUSOM reserves the right to rescind an offer of admission to any applicant still holding an active acceptance at another institution while having a “Commit to Enroll” status with TUSOM. TUSOM reserves the right to rescind offers of admission from any applicant still holding a TUSOM acceptance while indicating that they either “Plan to Enroll” or “Commit to Enroll” at another institution after April 30th. For applicants accepted after April 30th, the timeline for selecting “Plan to Enroll” will be specified by the Assistant Dean for Admissions.
All MD applicants planning to matriculate at TUSOM should select the “Commit to Enroll” option no later than one week before the first day of orientation. Should an applicant have an extenuating circumstance preventing compliance with this procedure, it is the applicant’s responsibility to notify the TUSOM Office of Admissions and seek an extension or exception.

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Tulane University School of Medicine has a societal responsibility to train competent healthcare providers and scientists who not only demonstrate robust medical knowledge and clinical skills but can appropriately apply their knowledge and skills to effectively interpret information and contribute to patient-centered decisions across a broad spectrum of medical situations and settings. To accomplish its mission, TUSOM has established a curriculum consisting of core courses and clerkships, required rotations, and elective rotations.  Although students learn and work under the supervision of the faculty, they interact with patients throughout their medical school education, and as such, patient safety and wellbeing are major factors in establishing technical requirements.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Scholarships and loans (federal, private, and Tulane programs) are available to students based on an analysis of the individual's financial needs. Additionally, each year approximately 30 students are awarded scholarships which are based on the student's academic record, leadership experience and community service.  Students do not have to apply for these scholarships as all admitted students are automatically considered for these awards.  For more information regarding financial aid: https://financialaid.tulane.edu/graduate/medicine

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: TUSOM does not have required prerequisites, but in general you will need to have a solid background in the sciences, including: biology, physics, chemistry, and mathematics.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Tulane University School of Medicine attracts a large number of applicants each year. Because we desire to have applicants who balance humanism and academic rigor, we have consistently encouraged applicants to pursue a broad education. In addition, we seek out applicants who have a wealth of life experiences. This requires a rigorous interdisciplinary pursuit of academics and of sciences and humanities. Applicants are highly encouraged to earn an undergraduate degree from a regionally accredited college or university by the time of matriculation. Because of the changes in the Medical College Admissions Test (MCAT), suggested preparation includes the social sciences and psychology.
